metadata.paper_title: Multi-step Consistency Models: Fast Generation with Theoretical Guarantees

phase_1_problem.global_context_latex: Forward process (OU): $dx_t = -x_t dt + \sqrt{2}dw_t$. Reverse PF-ODE: $dx_t = [-x_t - s_t(x_t)]dt$. Empirical ODE: $d\hat{x}_t = [-\hat{x}_t - \hat{s}_t(\hat{x}_t)]dt$. Consistency function $f(t', t, x_t)$ maps $x_t$ to $x_{t'}$. Multi-step sampling (Algorithm 1): $\hat{x}_{k-1} = e^{t_{k-1}^{\prime}-t_{k-1}}\hat{f}(t_{k-1}^{\prime}, t_k, \hat{x}_k) + \sqrt{1-e^{2(t_{k-1}^{\prime}-t_{k-1})}}z$. Assumptions: (1) $\mathbb{E}[\|\hat{s}_t - s_t\|^2] \le \epsilon_{score}^2$; (2) Finite 2nd moment $m_2$; (Note: This extraction focuses on the Non-Smooth case, so Lipschitz score assumption is removed).
phase_1_problem.main_goal_latex: Establish an upper bound for the KL divergence $KL(p_{t_0} || \hat{p}_{t_0})$ in the non-smooth setting. The bound should characterize the convergence rate with respect to the dimension $d$, total time $T$, and score estimation error $\epsilon_{score}$.

phase_2_planning_oracle.strategic_rationale: We adopt a divide-and-conquer strategy by decomposing the global error into initialization and cumulative discretization errors, then handling the non-smooth score function by bounding the trajectory deviation using Gaussian perturbation properties.

roadmap_steps.sub_goal_description: Given the multi-step sampling process, establish a decomposition of the global KL divergence into an initialization error term and a summation of step-wise conditional KL divergences.
Given the Gaussian transition kernels of the sampling algorithm, establish an explicit algebraic expression for the conditional KL divergence at a single step.
Given the error dynamics without Lipschitz assumptions, establish a bound on the trajectory deviation by exploiting the properties of Gaussian perturbations to control the score difference.
Given the trajectory bounds and initialization error, establish the final global convergence rate.

step_details.description: Decompose the KL divergence using the chain rule and data processing inequality.
Compute the specific KL divergence between two Gaussian distributions with shared covariance.

Construct the differential equation for the error $\Delta_t$. Use Young's inequality to separate terms, then apply specific bounds for non-smooth scores (Gaussian perturbation) and Gronwall's inequality.
Bound the initialization error using standard results for the OU process and sum the terms.
